Plan a crossed precision study for an LLM pipeline

Source: R/design.R
msa_design.Rd

Builds the run plan of a crossed measurement-system study: every item is processed under every prompt variant and every model, reps times per block. Items play the role of parts, prompt variants and models play the role of appraisers and instruments, replicates measure repeatability, and blocks separate replicates in time (different hours or days), which is necessary because inference endpoints are not deterministic at temperature 0 and their behaviour drifts with load.

Usage

msa_design(
  items,
  prompts,
  models,
  reps = 3,
  blocks = 1,
  order = c("random", "fixed"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

items

A character vector of item texts (optionally named by item id) or a data.frame with columns item_id and text. Additional columns (for example reference) are carried along and can be used as placeholders in prompts.

prompts

A character vector of prompt templates. Placeholders in braces are replaced by the item fields: {text} is always available, {item_id} and any other column of items can be used as well. Names become prompt ids (default P1, P2, ...).

models

A character vector of model identifiers passed to the backend. Names become model ids (default: the identifiers themselves).

reps

Number of replicates per item, prompt, model and block.

blocks

Number of blocks (sessions). Run each block at a different time to capture temporal drift of the endpoint.

order

"random" randomises the run order within each block (recommended), "fixed" keeps the crossing order.

seed

Optional seed for the randomisation.

Value

A data.frame of class msa_design with one row per planned call: block, position (run order within block), item_id, prompt_id, model_id, rep, prompt (the rendered prompt) and model (the backend model identifier). The design parameters are stored as attributes.

Examples

items <- c(v1 = "NM_000059.4:c.1813dupA", v2 = "NM_000059.4:c.7397T>C")
prompts <- c(
  short = "Classify the variant {text} according to ACMG/AMP. Answer with one class.",
  long  = "You are a clinical geneticist. Classify {text} (ACMG/AMP, 5 tiers)."
)
d <- msa_design(items, prompts, models = c("model-a", "model-b"), reps = 2, seed = 1)
head(d)
#> Crossed precision study for an LLM pipeline
#>   items (parts):      2
#>   prompt variants:    2  [short, long]
#>   models:             2  [model-a, model-b]
#>   replicates/block:   2
#>   blocks (sessions):  1
#>   planned calls:      6
#> 
#> First rows (prompt text truncated):
#>  block position item_id prompt_id model_id rep
#>      1        1      v2     short  model-a   1
#>      1        2      v1     short  model-b   2
#>      1        3      v1      long  model-b   1
#>      1        4      v1     short  model-a   1
#>      1        5      v1     short  model-a   2
#>      1        6      v2      long  model-a   2
#>                                       prompt   model
#>  Classify the variant NM_000059.4:c.7397T... model-a
#>  Classify the variant NM_000059.4:c.1813d... model-b
#>  You are a clinical geneticist. Classify ... model-b
#>  Classify the variant NM_000059.4:c.1813d... model-a
#>  Classify the variant NM_000059.4:c.1813d... model-a
#>  You are a clinical geneticist. Classify ... model-a
summary(d)
#> Crossed precision study for an LLM pipeline
#>   items (parts):      2
#>   prompt variants:    2  [short, long]
#>   models:             2  [model-a, model-b]
#>   replicates/block:   2
#>   blocks (sessions):  1
#>   planned calls:      16
